attacks.claim_at_risk: The sealed run could execute a different law or unofficial comparison.
attacks.method: Recomputed all 38 source hashes of frozen contract 6dac6c6fa68d2ce8d35a72fdccc89d4803d68795c76cd42fe8230ad75ea3a210. The shared runner verifies Python/package versions and the code/contract digest. Missing R1 was rejected on a direct no-execution trial.

attacks.claim_at_risk: Adaptive choices might use later growth, reference membership or reserved outcomes.
attacks.method: Inspected proposal, archive and scorer interfaces. Mutating all observations after the second round and changing a terminal status after that cut left the early reading unchanged on the fixed positive fixture. Source calibration and late-read collection are unavailable to the proposal routine.

attacks.claim_at_risk: Renamed or known public starts could contaminate the held-back population or serve as two witnesses.
attacks.method: Checked canonical coloring/incidence encoding, exact rejection of three public reference codes, modulo-five partition and per-arm duplicate rejection. The additional feature is tested on residue four only after a completed search summary. The independent symmetry count gives 864 pre-split identities.

attacks.claim_at_risk: Timing and reference privilege might favor either arm.
attacks.method: Both arms pay for selection, proposed sources, exact dual-law eligibility, growth, later readings and separate verification. Independent sampling shares the first proposal and the same admission/caps; execution order is randomized. Secondary replay clips at the smaller completed proposal count and repeats verification.

attacks.claim_at_risk: The compressed logs might lose data, or literal replay might fail on serialized extra meetings.
attacks.method: Independently decompressed the development ledger and compared all 21,748,154 bytes to its source. A fixed out-of-family extra-meeting founder survived JSON roundtrip through from_record and retained its canonical identity. Candidate verification rechecks literal holdings under renamed identities; raw attempts include eligibility and timing.

attacks.claim_at_risk: A repeat of one representation or a random signature outside a small dictionary might be called a new regime.
attacks.method: Distinct canonical founders within each run, still live through round five, with identical absent late signatures are required. Interpreted only relative to the frozen dictionary of 8 parity and 10 not-all-equal signatures from 128 admitted in 623 attempts plus public references.

attacks.claim_at_risk: A proposal count limit or uncharged archive bookkeeping could effectively give different CPU budgets.
attacks.method: Independently reconciled all 40 final development arms: each had exactly 80,000,000 ns search/50,000,000 ns verification, reached the CPU boundary, and its eligible rows totaled its claimed completions. The rejected earlier 2,048 ceiling was raised symmetrically before freeze to 16,384; secondary verification is explicitly charged outside the primary allowance.

attacks.claim_at_risk: Hundreds of proposals or reused validation pairs could masquerade as independent replications.
attacks.method: The primary unit is one paired run, 48 per law, with paired contrast and two-law multiplicity control. Finite reserve uses the product of founder masses within matched pairs and exact counting. Independently verified total base probability one and one sixth in each size/type stratum by symmetry counting.

attacks.claim_at_risk: Arbitrary labels or a different serialization might change discovery credit.
attacks.method: Exact permutation-minimization defines founder identity, bounded edits are re-qualified, and independent literal replay rebuilds holder and distinction names. Checked a frozen extra-meeting fixture after JSON serialization. Different mothers producing the same unlabelled source never provide independent witnesses.

attacks.claim_at_risk: More cheap duplicate proposals, cap censoring, or known single-birth continuations might create apparent diversity gains.
attacks.method: The design reports failures, repeated proposals, literal replay coverage, known closures, number of complete trajectories and a common-count sensitivity. The open-ended component is a finite fingerprint with a frozen reference; no new vocabulary selected after the run enters the score.

nonclaims: R1 authorizes the exact bounded execution only after the coordinating task confirms the Stage A prerequisite and releases Stage B. The fresh validation requires a complete search summary.
Process CPU is held fixed; completed proposal counts can vary across machines and are reported. CPU-limited outcomes do not guarantee a method advantage on other budgets.
